## Todo

Entries are in priority order, the first highest, and reprioritizing is moving an entry. Each is a
`###` heading, so a citation is a link to its anchor. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form).
Deeper detail goes in a `notes/` design file (link via `[N]` ref).

### feat: the project's tasks move to cargo xtask

(wink + agent, 2026-11-16) Validate, build, test, run, and install are the work's, a C project's
nothing like a Rust one's, and none of them is repo management, so they leave vc-x1 for the
project's own `cargo xtask`, which already bumps the version. Before **feat: a cycle's state is
recorded, and every end is durable**, by wink's call, sooner rather than later.

- **xtask gains the tasks**: `validate [--fast]`, `build`, `run`, and `install [--profile dev]`,
  the build's provenance, `VC_X1_BUILD_COMMIT` and `VC_X1_BUILD_STATE`, made by spawning `jj`,
  which xtask may since it is not vc-x1.
- **The profiles are Cargo's** (wink, 2026-11-16): a profile is a `Cargo.toml` `[profile.<name>]`,
  `dev` and `release` built in and any other, a soak's release candidate, declared there with
  `inherits`, and `.vc-config.md`'s `[profile.*]` tables go. xtask takes a profile by its Cargo
  name and keeps nothing beside it.
  - The `cargo` key is the name itself, and the binary's path is cargo's to say, `target/<profile
    dir>/<name>` from `cargo metadata`, `dev`'s directory being `debug`.
  - We think the install suffix is a rule, not a setting: `release` installs as `vc-x1` and every
    other profile as `vc-x1-<name>`, so `dev` keeps `vc-x1-dev`.
- **vc-x1 drops them**: its `validate`, `build`, `run`, and `install` and the `[validate]`,
  `[build]`, `[install]`, and `[profile.*]` tables go, each command refused with a pointer to
  `cargo xtask`, and the README's [Workspace config tables](README.md#workspace-config-tables)
  with them.
- **Who names them**: `CONTRIBUTING.md > ## Tasks`'s command column, its pointer to the config
  tables, and the agent-files' per-rung flow and `[validate]` sentence, rewritten to task names.
- **The family**: `vc-dr-apply`'s language skeleton stops writing `[validate]` and fills the
  `CONTRIBUTING.md` stub's tasks, the stub itself shipped by **docs: CONTRIBUTING.md names the
### feat: a cycle's state is recorded, and every end is durable

(wink + agent, 2026-11-15 and 16, from the dead-end **fix: a cycle commit marks no rung current**,
io-uring-x1's `m-13`, and zc-ring-x1's `m-14`) The cycle protocol's next form, folding the three
entries the dead-end filed, **feat: a rung's state is recorded in TODO.md**, **feat: a closing names
its shape, and its target once**, and **feat: a dead-end lands on a target or a tag**. vc-x1 infers
a cycle's commits from bookmark reachability, so a set-aside bookmark corrupted the ladder and the
commit count twice. `cycle --commit` writes the next rung `(current)`, a prediction. And a cycle
stopped early has no durable end, its agent commits' `ochid:` trailers left naming work commits no
pushed ref keeps. One cycle, its rungs below, wink's "we'll see how it goes".

- **The principle.** The repo holds what happened, and `TODO.md` holds where the cycle is going and
  which commit each finished rung is. Every stage checks that the two agree, and a disagreement
  stops it, neither side assumed right.
  - The one inference that goes is the branch revset: the cycle's commits are the change ids its
    record holds, each confirmed by the repo.
  - `zTOC.md`'s ladder is generated from the record by every cycle command, never edited by hand.
  - A session resumes from the record and the repo, never from a note: a cold acquaint knows where a
    cycle stands with nothing written for it by hand (wink, 2026-11-16).
- **The record.** A fenced `toml` block follows the `###` cycle heading, and one follows each
  `#####` rung heading once the rung has started.
  - The cycle block: `bookmark`, the cycle's one bookmark, `provisional = true` while that name is
    vc-x1's placeholder, and `state`, `done` or `dead-end`, added by the closing.
  - The rung block: `state`, one of `current`, `done`, or `dead-end`, `change`, the work commit's
    full change id for `done` and `dead-end`, and `agent-at`, the agent `@`'s commit id when the
    rung started, a commit id since it changes with every snapshot.
  - `current` and `agent-at` live in the working copy alone, `--commit` replacing them, so a commit
    holds `state` and `change` only.
  - No number is stored, the ladder numbering by position.

Run a cycle by its stages, each a flag, one command for the acts
the flow has.

--open opens a cycle: it makes the bookmark on the work @ first,
the slug of --title or --bookmark's name, kept local, then
writes the cycle's record. In TODO.md what `## Closed` holds is
deleted and the `## Todo` entry titled as --title is moved into an
`## In Progress` scaffold, an empty one when no entry matches, and
in zTOC.md the ladder is replaced with the opening and the closing.
Every check is made before anything changes: a cycle in progress is
refused, as is a name in use, and a workspace with no TODO.md or
zTOC.md, a cycle running on its record. --no-record makes the
bookmark alone, a branch the later stages will not take, as does
--bookmark without --title.
--dry-run says each edit and makes none. Nothing is committed or
pushed, and the version is the project's to bump.

--ladder makes the ladder in zTOC.md from the rung headings, the
`##### ` headings under `#### Rungs` of the cycle in progress in
TODO.md, in their order, so a rung is written once. Each line is
numbered by its position and its marker computed: `(done)` when a
commit of the rung's title is on the cycle's branch, `(current)` the
first without one. Refused, with nothing edited: a commit on the
branch that is no rung's, a rung written twice, a ladder not opened
and closed by the cycle title plus " opening" and " closing", and
a line of the ladder there that is no rung by its grammar. The
branch is the commits the cycle's bookmark reaches that no other
local bookmark does, the bookmark the title's slug or --bookmark's.

--commit commits the working copies as a rung of the cycle in
progress, by the code `vc-x1 commit` runs, so a dual workspace gets
the pair, each half stamped with the other's change id. A cycle's
first commit is its opening: the title is the cycle title plus
" opening" and the body `[opening] body`, a --body given taking
its place. Any other is a work rung, which gives --title, a rung
heading not yet committed, and --body, the text or @PATH. The ladder
is rewritten first, the rung done, so the commit carries it, and the
cycle's bookmark is the one advanced, no other. -s is required: `b`
the pair, `w` the work half alone, `p` a plain repo's commit, each
checked against the workspace. --push publishes the rung on the cycle's
bookmark, a
draft. The closing is not a rung's commit, and is refused.

--close [REV,...] closes the cycle from the work @, which is on the
cycle's tip, and names its shape, --single-step or --multi-step,
which the branch's commit count checks. --single-step is the cycle's
one commit: made now from @ when the branch has none, or the opening
with the closing squashed into it when it has one, its title the bare
cycle title and its trailer kept, and refused over two or more. Its
--body is required, the commit holding the work, unless
--default-body asks for the pointer. --multi-step is a ladder, whose
closing is its own commit, the cycle title plus " closing" and
`[closing] body` unless --title or --body is given, and refused with
no opening committed.
It is linear, on @'s own parents, unless --trapezoid <BOOKMARK> makes
the destination its first parent or a REV listed joins another
head, each a parent after @'s. --dead-end, with --multi-step, titles
the closing " dead-end closing". The ladder is rewritten, every
rung done, and the record moved to `## Closed`, both in the commit.
The acceptance check comes first, by hand, and again after.

--land <BOOKMARK> lands a closed cycle on the destination, any
bookmark, none assumed: the agent @
committed when the cycle's commits name it, the destination
fast-forwarded to the cycle's last commit, and the cycle's bookmark
deleted, --skip keeping a side. The cycle is the one `## Closed`
holds, its bookmark the title's slug or --bookmark's, and a cycle
still in progress is refused. A destination that moved is refused,
naming the ways on, and --merge is one: a merge commit of the
destination and the cycle's last commit, made from an empty @ and
then landed, a conflicted one undone and left to you. The stages
chain in their order, `cycle --close --multi-step --land <BOOKMARK> -s b
--push`, the
Land's checks made before the closing is. --push with --land
publishes the destination and deletes the cycle's bookmark on
origin, and without --land it is the draft push.

--push alone is a stage: it publishes what the cycle's state calls
for. A cycle in progress, or closed and not landed, is a draft, and
its bookmark is pushed. A cycle landed here publishes the target its
landmark is on and deletes the cycle's bookmark on origin, and with
nothing to publish it says so. -s is required, `b` or `p`.

--status says where the cycle stands and changes nothing: the
title, the bookmark and whether it is on the work @, the commits on
the branch and how many are not pushed, the ladder as the rungs and
the commits make it, a note when zTOC.md's differs, and the stage
that comes next. What another stage would refuse, it says.

  hold. Delete both in one cycle, after a sweep turns every link into them (Todo entries, the
  backlog, rationale.md, the other members' messages) into a permalink at the SHA before the
  deletion.
  - Waits on: **`vc-x1 closed "<title>"`** landed, and the session viewer good enough to read
    a cycle's record from the transcript.
  - Place when unblocked: first.
- **Sync's remote look stops spawning git.** (wink + agent, 2026-10-09) Sync learns where a
  remote's bookmarks are by spawning `git ls-remote`, and downloads the commits of the ones that
  moved by spawning a `git fetch` that moves no ref, the sixth entry of the spawn register in
  `clippy.toml` and the one spawn of `git`. Replace `git_command` and its two callers in
  `src/jj/session.rs` with jj-lib's query, delete the `#[allow]`, and close the entry.
  - Waits on: jj-lib's public API offering that query. Neither 0.45.1 nor 0.46.0 has one:
    `rg -i 'ls.remote' src/` in the jj-lib source prints nothing, and its git subprocess layer is
    `pub(crate)`. An upstream feature request, once filed or found, is named here.
  - Place when unblocked: first, being one function.
- **lookup matches a line to its write by content.** (wink + agent, 2026-10-26) lookup resolves a
  line through blame to its commit and the commit's `ochid:` trailer to its agent partner, with
  the agent commits inside a time tolerance as candidates when there is no trailer. In one
  person's workspace the trailer is exact. In a shared repo it fails: a squash or rebase merge
  leaves blame on a commit no trailer names, and a trailer that survives may point into an
  agent-repo the reader cannot reach. Time fails too, many contributors' commits inside any
  tolerance.
  - The key that survives squash, rebase, and cherry-pick is the text: each transcript records
    what every Write and Edit put into a file, so a line is matched to the call that wrote it
    with no commit between. **dr1_every_committed_line_finds_its_transcript_write** checks a
    part of it. The layering: the trailer when it resolves, the content when it does not, time
    last.
  - What makes it hard: a line changed after the write, by a person or `cargo fmt`, needs a
    fuzzy match, a common line (`}`, `Ok(())`) needs its hunk for context, and every
    contributor's transcripts must be reachable and indexed, a privacy question as much as a
    technical one.

    arises there.

[package]
name = "xtask"
version = "0.0.0"
edition = "2024"
publish = false

# The project's own tasks, run by `cargo xtask <task>`, the alias in
# `.cargo/config.toml`. Outside `vc-x1`, which knows nothing of the
# work: the version and its bump are the project's.

[dependencies]

clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "wrap_help"] }

# `cargo xtask <task>` runs the project's own tasks, the `xtask`

xtask = "run --quiet --package xtask --"

## Suffix scheme

The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
Preparation**.

This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
step without renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between
- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of every step (the per-commit checklist carries the step),
so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
commit carries a distinct version. The bump is the project's, by its own tool, and `vc-x1` never
writes a version: with `[version] file` and `pattern` in the config it refuses a commit that
leaves the version's line unchanged, and `--same-version` commits it as it is.

## Agent-files version

The agent-files set has a version of its own, apart from the artifact's, so which set an adopter
carries is read from a listing rather than a diff, and an `agent-files` title has a token that is
unique by construction ([Project-declared types](prose.md#project-declared-types),
[why](rationale.md#agent-files-version)).

- **Record**: an empty file, `agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z{-suffix}`, the version its name. `ls
  agent-data` shows it without a read, a bump is a rename, and
  `git log --diff-filter=A -- 'agent-data/agent-files-v*'` lists every version beside the commit
  that introduced it.
- **Spelling**: `vX.Y.Z` everywhere the agent-files version is written, the file name, an
  `agent-files` title, and vc-x1's output, so `agent-files v0.1.0` reads the same in all three. The
  `v` is the name-plus-version pair as cargo prints it (`bar v1.0.0`), and a tool's own banner stays
  bare (`vc-x1 0.82.0`), so a `v` number is the set's and a bare one the artifact's.
- **Proposals bump, adoptions copy**: a proposal cycle bumps it at the opening, advancing per
  [Advancing X.Y.Z](#advancing-xyz-patch-by-default), and its rungs walk the [Suffix
  scheme](#suffix-scheme) beside the artifact's version, `-0`, `-1`, then bare at the close-out, so
  a set copied from a draft bookmark says on its face that it is unfinished. An adoption copies the
  source's bare file and bumps nothing.
- **An adoption is a copy and a check**: `vc-x1 agent-files copy --from <src>` takes the set, and
  `vc-x1 agent-files diff --from <src>` is the adoption's last act, exiting zero when the two copies
  are the same and printing the differences the acceptance agreed to when they are not.
- **Named by the proposal**: a version names the text as proposed. An adopter that accepts with
  changes carries them as its diff against that text, and two proposers claiming one number are
  two proposals, the later re-proposing under the next.
- **Which digit**: tend toward the patch digit, kept to one digit and rolled over into the minor.
  We think the minor stays within two digits and major increments when a proposal says so.
